question: What physical activity advice should a nurse give?

options.A: Participate in heavy weightlifting daily
options.B: Engage in gentle, graduated exercise like walking
options.C: Only exercise when experiencing severe exhaustion
options.D: Avoid all forms of movement until fully recovered

explanation: Awesome job! Slow and steady exercise like walking boosts mood and stamina without draining their low energy reserves. You're ready for the wards! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T9#GNS314_U2_T9_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge facing mental health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Widespread social stigma preventing early treatment seeking
options.B: Severe shortages of trained psychiatric nurses and doctors
options.C: Inadequate government funding for healthcare infrastructure
options.D: A complete absence of mental health conditions in the population

explanation: You got it! Mental health issues are very much present in Nigeria. The real roadblocks are stigma, staff shortages, and poor funding—not a lack of illnesses. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T9#GNS314_U1_T9_h6)

question: Which group is considered a trusted source of health education within local communities?

options.A: Real estate agents
options.B: Construction workers
options.C: Nurses
options.D: Financial auditors

explanation: Nurses hold a high level of public trust, which makes community members more likely to listen to and follow their safety guidance. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T9#GNS315_U5_T9_h2)

question: Which pathway carries nerve signals toward the central nervous system?

options.A: Sympathetic division
options.B: Efferent division
options.C: Afferent division
options.D: Autonomic division

explanation: A-fferent arrives at the brain (think 'A' for arrival). You'll master these terms in no time! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h4)

question: Why might an adolescent with untreated depression turn to substance abuse?

options.A: To cure a bacterial infection
options.B: To improve their school grades permanently
options.C: To self-medicate and escape emotional pain
options.D: To strengthen their immune system

explanation: Teens struggling with mental health issues like depression often use drugs or alcohol as an unhealthy way to cope with overwhelming emotional distress. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T13#GNS312_U3_T13_h3)

question: Why must nurses look at published research with a critical eye?

options.A: Research studies are only meant for academic promotion
options.B: Hospital management requires nurses to rewrite journal articles
options.C: Authors purposely hide their results to confuse readers
options.D: Not all published studies are designed or conducted well

explanation: Even peer-reviewed journals can contain flaws, so nurses must evaluate the evidence before applying it to patients. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is pre-contraception counseling so important in family planning clinics?

options.A: It is legally required before a patient can purchase over-the-counter condoms
options.B: It permanently prevents users from ever changing their chosen method
options.C: It helps clients choose a method that suits their lifestyle while addressing fears or myths
options.D: It replaces the need for any physical health assessment by a doctor

explanation: You nailed it! Good counseling clears up rumors about side effects and helps clients find the contraceptive method that best fits their personal life. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h3)

question: What does patient autonomy mean during medication administration?

options.A: The doctor takes full responsibility for the patient's diet
options.B: The patient has the right to make informed choices about their drugs
options.C: The hospital pharmacy controls all drug distribution
options.D: The nurse decides the best time to give every pill

explanation: Autonomy is the ethical principle that protects a person's right to choose or refuse medical treatments after being fully informed. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h2)

question: A patient keeps asking you to repeat yourself and turns one ear toward you when you speak. What is your best next nursing action?

options.A: Document that the patient has complete and permanent sensorineural deafness
options.B: Disregard the observation as a normal sign of aging requiring no action
options.C: Perform a focused auditory assessment and check for cerumen impaction
options.D: Refer the patient immediately for urgent visual acuity testing

explanation: Always start with simple nursing assessments first! Looking for a simple wax buildup (cerumen impaction) or checking hearing function is a great practical step before jumping to major conclusions. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T8#GNS311_U3_T8_h2)

question: Which computer system is strong enough to host an entire hospital's electronic health record database?

options.A: Pocket smartphone
options.B: Mainframe computer
options.C: Personal desktop
options.D: Analog signal monitor

explanation: That's right! Mainframes have the immense power needed to keep a whole hospital's database running smoothly and securely. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T6#GNS113_U1_T6_h5)

question: Which of these is true about human resilience?

options.A: It only exists in professional athletes
options.B: It can be cultivated and developed over time
options.C: It disappears entirely after childhood
options.D: It is completely fixed at the time of birth

explanation: Resilience isn't something you're just born with. Like a muscle, it grows stronger with practice, good support, and coping skills. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h8)

question: How does severe protein-energy malnutrition directly weaken a person's immune system?

options.A: By depriving the body of building blocks needed to make immune cells and antibodies
options.B: By stopping the liver from producing digestive enzymes
options.C: By destroying red blood cells in the spleen
options.D: By increasing blood pressure too quickly for white cells to circulate

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Just like you need blocks to build a house, your body needs protein to build antibodies and white blood cells. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h4)

question: Which part of the brain houses the front sections (anterior horns) of the lateral ventricles?

options.A: Frontal lobes
options.B: Occipital lobes
options.C: Temporal lobes
options.D: Cerebellar lobes

explanation: Spot on! The front part of the lateral ventricle reaches forward right into the frontal lobe of the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h2)

question: A senior nurse angrily complains during a meeting about new shift scheduling software. What does her anger usually mean?

options.A: She is trying to get her younger colleagues fired from the unit.
options.B: She is feeling vulnerable and cares about her daily workflow.
options.C: She completely lacks basic computer literacy skills.
options.D: She is planning to resign from the hospital by the end of the week.

explanation: Anger during big changes often masks vulnerability. It shows she deeply cares about how her work gets done! [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h4)

question: How can a high-protein diet affect a patient who already has chronic kidney disease?

options.A: It replaces the need for routine blood tests
options.B: It has zero impact on their renal system
options.C: It completely cures their kidney disease within weeks
options.D: It can accelerate the decline of their kidney function

explanation: Struggling kidneys find it hard to filter heavy loads of nitrogen waste. For CKD patients, too much protein can actually make their kidney damage worse. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h7)

question: What is the main reason we use diagnostic devices in healthcare?

options.A: To permanently cure chronic illnesses
options.B: To replace the need for physical assessments
options.C: To detect diseases and monitor health conditions
options.D: To replace human clinical judgment entirely

explanation: You've got this! Diagnostic tools simply help us gather clear facts so we can identify and track health issues. Great job starting here! [learn more](GNS113_U4_T1#GNS113_U4_T1_h1)

question: A nurse uses a bedside scanner to check a patient's wristband and a medication package before giving a pill. What safety feature is being used?

options.A: Barcode medication administration
options.B: Computerized provider order entry
options.C: Health information exchange network
options.D: Clinical decision support alerts

explanation: Scanning patient wristbands and medication packages prevents administration errors by verifying the right patient, drug, and dose. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why are shellfish like shrimp and crabs not allowed in a traditional kosher diet?

options.A: They are classified as land animals
options.B: They are harvested during forbidden months
options.C: They consume blood from other marine life
options.D: They lack fins and scales

explanation: According to kosher rules, acceptable seafood must have both fins and scales, which rules out bottom-feeding shellfish like crabs and shrimp. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T019#GNS227_U2_T019_h4)

question: Which acronym represents the four main stages of pharmacokinetics?

options.A: ABCS
options.B: DOME
options.C: FAST
options.D: ADME

explanation: ADME is your best friend here! It stands for Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion. Memorize this, and pharmacology topics become much easier. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is it better to offer simple, closed choices rather than open-ended questions when talking to a dementia patient?

options.A: It reduces the mental effort required to process and answer the question
options.B: It ensures the patient always drinks water instead of sugary beverages
options.C: It allows the nurse to maintain strict control over the daily routine
options.D: It prevents the patient from changing their mind later in the day

explanation: Think of it like saving phone battery! Open questions can overwhelm a tired or confused brain, whereas 'Would you like tea or water?' is much easier to answer. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T10#GNS324_U4_T10_h4)

question: Besides giving us shape, what important minerals do our bones store for the body?

options.A: Calcium and phosphorus
options.B: Iron and magnesium
options.C: Sodium and chloride
options.D: Potassium and zinc

explanation: Think of your bones as a savings bank! They store vital minerals like calcium and phosphorus, releasing them into your bloodstream whenever your body needs a top-up. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T1#GNS222_U1_T1_h1)

question: In the common obstetric history acronym TPAL, what does the letter 'P' stand for?

options.A: Pelvic diameter
options.B: Primary contractions
options.C: Preterm births
options.D: Placental position

explanation: In TPAL, P stands for preterm births—deliveries that happen before 37 completed weeks of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h4)

question: What term describes the swallowing difficulties caused by muscle weakness in degenerative disorders?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Aphasia
options.C: Dysarthria
options.D: Dysphagia

explanation: Dysphagia is the medical term for difficulty swallowing—something we must watch out for closely to prevent food or liquid from entering the airway. You're doing awesome! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h6)

question: Why do patients in severe anaphylaxis often feel dizzy or faint?

options.A: Blood pressure crashes because fluid leaks out of widened blood vessels
options.B: Heavy sweating causes bad dehydration
options.C: The brain gets too much oxygen from fast breathing
options.D: The heart beats too slowly to pump blood

explanation: Blood vessels suddenly open wide and leak fluid, causing blood pressure to drop low. This starves the brain of blood flow, leading to dizziness. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is the main goal of nursing research?

options.A: To increase the financial revenue of private health institutions
options.B: To replace traditional medical diagnoses with nursing diagnoses
options.C: To build a knowledge base that guides practice and improves patient outcomes
options.D: To reduce the administrative workload of hospital managers

explanation: Spot on! Nursing research is all about finding out what works best so we can give our patients the safest, highest quality care possible. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T6#GNS217_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is the primary job of an Institutional Review Board (IRB)?

options.A: Securing big money grants for labs
options.B: Writing nursing textbooks
options.C: Marketing new drugs to hospitals
options.D: Protecting the rights and safety of human research participants

explanation: Spot on! The IRB acts as a safety shield to ensure human subjects are treated ethically and safely. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T19#GNS224_U1_T19_h6)

question: What is the primary focus of modern occupational health nursing?

options.A: Promoting and protecting worker well-being
options.B: Providing long-term hospital bedside care
options.C: Designing factory machinery and tools
options.D: Managing corporate financial portfolios

explanation: Occupational health nursing centers on safeguarding the health, safety, and overall well-being of employees across various work environments. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h1)

question: As time went on, what sadly happened to many early asylums?

options.A: They became exclusive schools for young healers
options.B: They transformed into modern research hospitals
options.C: They closed down completely within a decade
options.D: They became overcrowded and abusive warehouses

explanation: Because of bad funding and too many patients, these places quickly went from being safe havens to centers full of neglect and poor treatment. So sad, but true history! [learn more](GNS314_U1_T4#GNS314_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why do we give a routine injection of Vitamin K to all newborns shortly after birth?

options.A: To boost their appetite for milk
options.B: To prevent dangerous bleeding since their clotting factors are low
options.C: To protect against hepatitis B
options.D: To protect against eye infections from the birth canal

explanation: Babies are born with sterile bellies that haven't built up the gut bacteria needed to make Vitamin K yet, putting them at risk for bleeding until feeding gets going. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h7)

question: How should a nurse manager respond when a staff member makes an honest, unintentional calculation slip?

options.A: Ignore the incident since no patient was actually harmed
options.B: Immediately terminate the nurse to set an example for others
options.C: Provide comfort and look at ways to improve the system
options.D: Report the nurse to the police for criminal negligence

explanation: Spot on! In a Just Culture, honest human error calls for support and system fixes, not unfair punishment. Learning is a journey! [learn more](GST319_U5_T6#GST319_U5_T6_h4)

question: When should you start doing a secondary survey on an emergency patient?

options.A: At the exact same time the primary survey starts
options.B: Only after the patient has been admitted to the main ward
options.C: After life-threatening conditions in the primary survey are stabilized
options.D: Before checking the patient's airway or breathing status

explanation: Spot on! Always tackle the life threats (Airway, Breathing, Circulation) first before doing a head-to-toe secondary check. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why is the cerebral aqueduct considered a high-risk spot for fluid blockage?

options.A: It contains sharp bony ridges that can cut surrounding neural tissue
options.B: It generates most of the cellular waste found in the brain
options.C: It pumps blood backward into the arterial system during high stress
options.D: Its narrow diameter makes it very prone to complete blockage from swelling

explanation: Spot on! Because it is the slimmest passage in the brain's plumbing system, even a tiny bit of swelling can easily block the flow. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h4)

question: What is a major social reason families continue to practice FGM?

options.A: Compliance with international health mandates
options.B: A direct recommendation by the national medical association
options.C: The prevention of childhood infectious diseases
options.D: Fear of social exclusion and unmarriageability

explanation: Sadly, many families do it because they fear their daughters will be rejected by the community or struggle to find husbands. Understanding this helps you treat patients with empathy. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T2#GNS312_U1_T2_h3)

question: What happens to the marks on daily tally sheets at the end of a clinic day?

options.A: The marks are counted and transferred into monthly summary registers
options.B: The tally marks are erased so the sheet can be reused tomorrow
options.C: The papers are burned to protect patient confidentiality
options.D: The sheets are mailed directly to the international health organization

explanation: Spot on! At the end of the day, we count up the tally marks so they can feed into our bigger monthly summary books and reports. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T13#GNS225_U2_T13_h4)

question: Which infection is a nurse most afraid of contracting after an accidental needle stick injury?

options.A: Tuberculosis
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Malaria

explanation: That's right! Blood-borne viruses like Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV are our biggest concerns after a sharp injury. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T16#GNS122_U3_T16_h6)

question: Which of the following is considered a vector in disease transmission?

options.A: A shared towel
options.B: A contaminated well
options.C: A mosquito
options.D: A surgical scalpel

explanation: Mosquitoes are living organisms that actively transmit disease agents like malaria parasites between hosts, making them classic biological vectors. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h5)

question: When wrapping a residual limb with an elastic bandage, where should the pressure be tightest?

options.A: At the bottom end of the stump
options.B: Equally tight all the way up
options.C: Near the top of the joint
options.D: Across the middle portion

explanation: Wrapping tighter at the bottom (distal end) pushes fluid upward and helps shape the limb into a neat cone, which makes fitting a prosthesis much easier later. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h4)

question: Why should you pinch the tip of a male condom before rolling it on?

options.A: To stop the penis from losing its erection
options.B: To activate the spermicidal lubricant
options.C: To leave space for semen and prevent bursting
options.D: To warm up the latex material

explanation: You got it! Pinching the tip pushes out trapped air and leaves a little room to catch the semen so the condom doesn't tear. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h4)

question: Where does a National Health Insurance Scheme usually get most of its money from?

options.A: Direct cash payments at hospital front desks
options.B: Government taxes and payroll deductions
options.C: Voluntary donations from local businesses
options.D: Monthly loans from commercial banks

explanation: That's correct! National schemes rely on public funds like taxes and mandatory employee contributions to make sure care stays available for everyone. [learn more](GST322_U4_T7#GST322_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why are temporary leave policies considered clinical interventions rather than just rewards?

options.A: They allow the hospital to permanently reduce bed capacity
options.B: They actively test the patient's coping and medication management skills outside the hospital
options.C: They prove to the court that the patient no longer needs medication
options.D: They force family members to take over full financial responsibility

explanation: Think of leave as a practical test! It helps us see how well a patient handles daily life and takes their medications outside the hospital walls. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h1)

question: What usually happens when a patient is discharged with a poor transition plan?

options.A: Instant recovery and permanent stability
options.B: Complete independence from all health services
options.C: Immediate employment in high-stress jobs
options.D: Rapid re-hospitalization or trouble with the law

explanation: Sadly, yes. Without proper support and follow-up in the community, patients often experience a relapse that brings them right back to the hospital or justice system. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T8#GNS314_U5_T8_h3)

question: In what way do nurses act as safety guards when using an EHR system?

options.A: By reviewing computerized alerts and verifying medication orders
options.B: By writing paper security codes on the walls of patient wards
options.C: By restricting doctors from ordering any laboratory tests
options.D: By physically repairing broken computer keyboards and monitors

explanation: Nurses use their clinical judgment alongside system prompts to catch potential errors before they reach the patient. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why do esophageal varices develop in patients with portal hypertension?

options.A: Blood backs up and forces open alternative collateral channels connecting portal and systemic veins
options.B: High stomach acid burns through the protective mucosal barrier of the esophagus
options.C: Swallowed food scraps scrape against the lining of the stomach and damage blood vessels
options.D: The liver releases excess clotting factors that clog small blood vessels near the throat

explanation: When the main gateway to the liver is blocked by high pressure, blood looks for alternative escape routes. It forces open smaller, fragile veins around the esophagus, causing them to bulge out like balloons (varices). [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is the most common way people get poisoned right inside their own homes?

options.A: Ingestion
options.B: Injection
options.C: Inhalation
options.D: Absorption

explanation: Well done! Swallowing things—like accidental medications or household cleaners—is by far the top way poisoning happens at home. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T14#GNS221_U3_T14_h2)

question: Which hormone directly triggers the tiny muscles around the milk glands to squeeze milk out during the let-down reflex?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Oxytocin is the 'let-down' hormone. When the baby suckles, oxytocin makes the tiny muscle-like cells (myoepithelial cells) squeeze the milk down the ducts. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h5)

question: Why do emergency personnel perform debridement on a ragged, torn wound before stitching it?

options.A: It makes the skin numb to the pain of the needle
options.B: Dead tissue delays healing and easily breeds bacteria
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling nervous
options.D: It stretches the skin so fewer stitches are needed

explanation: Removing non-viable tissue leaves only healthy, bleeding tissue that can heal rapidly and resist infection. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why is regular follow-up care essential for a patient recovering from hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: To monitor her weight, hydration, and lab values for stability
options.B: To measure the exact length of the baby using a tape measure
options.C: To make sure she is exercising at the gym twice a week
options.D: To change her prescribed prenatal vitamins every single week

explanation: Frequent checks allow healthcare providers to catch returning dehydration or weight loss early before hospitalization becomes necessary. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a limitation of using BMI in clinical practice?

options.A: It does not account for changes during pregnancy
options.B: It measures exact fat distribution in the arms
options.C: It can be misleading for elderly patients losing muscle
options.D: It fails to separate muscle weight from fat weight

explanation: BMI doesn't measure fat distribution or target specific body parts like arms; it's just a single ratio of total weight to height. Brilliant! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h5)

question: What CD4+ cell count threshold defines the progression from HIV infection to AIDS?

options.A: Below 50 cells per microliter
options.B: Below 200 cells per microliter
options.C: Below 500 cells per microliter
options.D: Below 1000 cells per microliter

explanation: Correct! Once the CD4+ count drops below 200 cells per microliter, the condition is classified as AIDS, indicating severe immune suppression. [learn more](GST114_U4_T11#GST114_U4_T11_h3)

question: Globally, where does the highest burden of unsafe medical care usually happen?

options.A: Rural community pharmacies in wealthy nations
options.B: Private specialized clinics in Europe
options.C: Advanced research hospitals in North America
options.D: Low- and middle-income countries

explanation: Resource-limited settings face tough system challenges that unfortunately lead to higher rates of preventable harm. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T8#GNS312_U5_T8_h2)

question: How might a patient react spiritually after suffering a severe physical impairment?

options.A: They strictly rely on medical textbooks to find inner peace
options.B: They universally abandon all religious thoughts and practices forever
options.C: They may either find deeper comfort in faith or feel abandoned by God
options.D: They automatically experience a complete resolution of existential doubt

explanation: Everyone copes differently. Some lean into their faith for strength, while others might feel angry or let down. Both reactions are very human. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T13#GNS225_U5_T13_h2)

question: Which of these is a bad practice that can cause tissue damage when giving injections?

options.A: Rotating sites when patients need repeated doses
options.B: Using the correct needle length for the patient's size
options.C: Giving multiple injections into the exact same spot
options.D: Allowing the skin disinfectant to dry before piercing

explanation: Spot on! Poking the exact same spot over and over causes hard, damaged tissue and scars. Always rotate your injection sites to give the skin and muscle a break! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T6#GNS125_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the main concern of 'statistical conclusion validity'?

options.A: Whether the hospital management approved the budget
options.B: Whether the results can be used in other countries
options.C: Whether participants signed their consent forms
options.D: Whether the right math and statistical tests were used to find a true link

explanation: This type of validity makes sure the researchers didn't use the wrong math formulas, so we can trust that their numbers actually mean something. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T26#GNS224_U1_T26_h5)

question: Why is a risk assessment done before holding a mass gathering?

options.A: To reduce ticket prices for attendees
options.B: To eliminate the need for any on-site security personnel
options.C: To identify potential hazards and plan appropriate medical and safety responses
options.D: To guarantee that the event makes a substantial financial profit

explanation: Spotting trouble spots beforehand means we can get medical help and safety measures ready before any emergency strikes. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T3#GNS315_U3_T3_h3)

question: Why must researchers follow a standardized procedure during data collection?

options.A: To make the research process take longer
options.B: To avoid getting permission from the hospital
options.C: To ensure patients pay for their participation
options.D: To prevent outside disturbances from ruining results

explanation: Standardized procedures ensure every participant has the same experience, keeping data collection consistent and reliable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of an Information Retrieval System in nursing?

options.A: To write nursing care plans without human input
options.B: To store, organize, and quickly find relevant clinical data
options.C: To automatically diagnose complex patient illnesses
options.D: To track daily hospital staff attendance records

explanation: An IRS is built specifically to help users locate stored information like research papers and clinical guidelines out of massive databases. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T8#GNS113_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is the very first priority when managing a patient who presents with acute shock?

options.A: Restoring adequate airway, breathing, and circulation
options.B: Preparing the patient for major exploratory surgery
options.C: Lowering the body temperature with cooling blankets
options.D: Administering broad-spectrum oral antibiotics immediately

explanation: Always remember your ABCs! No matter what kind of shock it is, emergency care always starts with securing the airway, breathing, and circulation before digging into secondary causes. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h6)

question: What happens when stock levels drop below a safe minimum in an electronic inventory system?

options.A: An automatic reorder alert is generated
options.B: The hospital power generator shuts down automatically
options.C: All patient charts are locked until new stock arrives
options.D: The nursing supervisor's license is suspended

explanation: Electronic systems track thresholds and notify purchasing staff to reorder items before they run out completely. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T5#GNS113_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a nasogastric tube?

options.A: To provide continuous oxygen to the lungs
options.B: To deliver liquid nutrients directly into the stomach
options.C: To drain excess urine from the bladder
options.D: To remove harmful toxins from the bloodstream

explanation: A nasogastric tube is passed through the nose into the stomach to supply food and medications when a patient cannot swallow safely. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T2#GNS212_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the primary physiological cause of fainting?

options.A: A sudden temporary drop in blood flow to the brain
options.B: An acute electrical storm in the brain tissue
options.C: A permanent blockage of the carotid arteries
options.D: A severe deficiency of potassium in the blood

explanation: Fainting happens when cerebral blood flow drops briefly, starving the brain of oxygen and glucose. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T16#GNS123_U3_T16_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a typical reason to call a Rapid Response Team?

options.A: A sudden drop in oxygen saturation
options.B: Unexplained chest pain or pressure
options.C: A patient complaining of mild boredom
options.D: A sudden decrease in mental alertness

explanation: You've got this! Feeling bored is uncomfortable, but it isn't an emergency. Oxygen drops, chest pain, and sudden confusion, however, are major warning signs that need immediate backup! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T11#GNS123_U5_T11_h6)

question: Why should a nurse spend some time talking to a teenage patient alone during a health checkup?

options.A: To legally remove parental consent for all future medical treatments
options.B: To prevent the parents from hearing about routine vaccination schedules

question: What is the most important fluid instruction to give a patient taking an expectorant?

question: What is a major advantage of field research over laboratory research?

question: Why is a high participant dropout rate a big problem in a longitudinal study?

question: What is one of the main goals of a nurse acting as a patient advocate in reproductive health?

options.D: Setting insurance premiums for fertility clinics

question: Why are the standard 'rights' of medication administration so important if a legal case of negligence arises?

question: How does the placenta give a newborn temporary protection against common infections?

question: What do we mean by the term 'gender roles'?

options.D: The biological hormones produced by the endocrine glands

question: Why is self-care considered a professional duty for nurses working in disaster zones?

question: Why does an RCA team repeatedly ask 'why' an incident occurred?

options.B: To prove that the patient contributed to their own injury
options.C: To interrogate nurses until they admit fault for their careless actions
options.D: To trace the chain of events back to the fundamental systemic breakdown

explanation: Asking 'why' multiple times peels back superficial layers of error to expose the real root cause in the workflow or environment. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h4)

question: Why is avoiding power struggles important when caring for a patient with a personality challenge?

options.A: Arguing escalates tension and rarely changes rigid behavioral patterns
options.B: Patients with personality challenges lack the ability to hear human voices
options.C: Patients always win arguments because nurses are legally not allowed to speak
options.D: Winning a power struggle cures the patient's underlying psychiatric condition instantly

question: What does gender-based violence (GBV) mean in simple terms?

question: How does drying (dehydration) primarily preserve food?

options.A: By keeping the food at freezing cold temperatures
options.B: By increasing the internal oxygen levels of the food
options.C: By adding large amounts of chemical preservatives
options.D: By removing the water that microorganisms need to grow

question: What is the medical term for difficulty swallowing, which is common in some older adults?

question: Why is finding the reservoir so important when there's a disease outbreak?

question: Which of these is a key frontline duty for a community health nurse in disease control?

question: What is the best position for transporting an unconscious patient who is still breathing and has a pulse?

question: What is the very first thing a nurse should figure out before teaching a patient at home?

question: A patient in contact isolation feels depressed and refuses to open their door for nursing care. What is your best action as a nurse?

options.B: Threaten to discharge the patient immediately if they do not cooperate with rules
options.C: Acknowledge their feelings, explain the care plan patiently, and spend extra social time with them

question: Why do waterborne diseases like cholera often spike during the rainy season in many Nigerian communities?

question: What is a great quality to look for when picking members for a QI team?

question: Where do raw vegetables usually pick up dirt and bacterial spores?

question: A nurse is packing a vaccine carrier for an outreach. What must be avoided to protect the vaccines?

question: Why does wearing the correct glove size matter so much in clinical work?

question: What part do environmental factors play in kicking off an autoimmune disease?

question: What is the most crucial check a nurse must perform before giving a scheduled dose of propranolol?

question: What is the common medical term for a nosebleed originating from the anterior nasal septum?

question: What is the very first step in the formal healthcare planning process?

question: Why is asking for healthcare different from buying regular everyday goods like shoes or food?

question: How does water move from inside the gut into the bloodstream during oral rehydration?

question: How does Quality Assurance differ from simple quality control?

question: In simple terms, what does the diathesis-stress model explain?

question: What is the main purpose of Koch's postulates?

question: What is the main purpose of delivering a shock with an Automated External Defibrillator (AED)?

question: A rural community suffers from a high rate of waterborne diseases like cholera. Besides treating sick patients, which action represents true intersectoral collaboration?

question: What is direct nursing delivery technology mainly used for?

question: Which type of food is best for adding bulk to stool and keeping constipation away?

question: Who is typically a member of a Health Facility Development Committee?

question: What is an important safety tip for any patient taking a medication that causes drowsiness?

question: Why is it so helpful to know a patient's past surgical history?

question: What is the main purpose of an assisted living facility?

question: What is a fomite?

question: What is the main job of the internal male reproductive organs altogether?

question: You are about to flush out a deep infected wound that might splash fluid. What PPE do you need to wear?

question: Which complication can happen if an unsterile herbal poultice is placed over a minor skin scratch?

question: What is the main job of a secondary literature source?

question: A nurse forgets to give a scheduled medication dose, realizes it hours later, and decides not to chart anything to avoid trouble. What legal risk does this create?

question: How does keeping a food diary differ from doing a 24-hour dietary recall?

question: Why should you stay right by the patient's side until they swallow their oral pills?

question: How does maintaining strict confidentiality during post-abortion counseling help the patient?

question: What is the primary normal function of synovial fluid in a healthy joint?

question: An instructor wants to use adult learning principles when teaching IV cannulation. What's the best way to do it?

question: Which factor is most important when deciding if a medicine belongs on an essential drug list?

question: What is the main role of a nurse when it comes to ward medical supplies?

question: Why do we keep the head of the bed slightly elevated for a patient with increased intracranial pressure from encephalitis?

question: What is the main goal of a nursing journal club in a hospital?

question: Why should you avoid putting too much text on a single PowerPoint slide?

question: What is the main goal of a public-private partnership (PPP) in healthcare?

question: Why should non-selective beta-blockers be used very carefully in patients with asthma?

question: What is a reliable way to check how severe a patient's fatigue really is?

question: What is an important duty for a nurse after a client joins a workshop?

question: Why can giving too much normal saline be harmful to a patient with uncontrolled internal bleeding?

question: Why are chemotherapy drugs considered dangerous for the nurses who handle them?

options.C: They cause immediate fainting if the nurse smells them

question: Why is preventing hypothermia so crucial when treating trauma victims?

question: How do open, uncovered infectious waste bins help spread diseases in the community?

question: Why can resistance from experienced staff make it hard to introduce EHR systems?

question: How does individualizing a medication schedule help a patient?

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention in cardiovascular care?

question: You need to put an IV line on a frightened preschooler. What is the best approach?

question: A patient recovering from a leg fracture is frustrated and feels like giving up. Which rehabilitation goal addresses this?

question: How does geriatric nursing differ from general gerontology?

question: Why do nurses and doctors gather information from multiple sources (like parents and teachers) during a child's psychiatric assessment?

options.C: Unusual bleeding or discharge
options.D: Ulceration of the skin

explanation: Remember CAUTION! The 'U' reminds us to never ignore unexplained bleeding or discharge from any part of the body. Keep that in your nursing toolkit! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T15#GNS214_U1_T15_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To ensure a continuous supply of affordable essential drugs
options.B: To provide free medical care to all indigent citizens
options.C: To fund the construction of new hospital wards and buildings
options.D: To generate heavy profits for the hospital management board

explanation: Think of the DRF as a self-sustaining cycle. Its main job is to make sure essential drugs never run out in the hospital pharmacy, so patients can always get what they need at a fair price! [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge facing healthcare collaboration in Nigeria?

options.A: Abundant medical supplies and excessive staffing levels
options.B: Inadequate infrastructure and fragmented record-keeping systems
options.C: Deep-seated professional hierarchies and historical power imbalances
options.D: Inter-professional rivalry between different healthcare worker groups

explanation: Correct! Nigeria's healthcare system unfortunately battles with shortages, not an excess of staff or medical supplies. [learn more](GST321_U7_T3#GST321_U7_T3_h5)

question: Why do nurses train local leaders and teachers in mental health first aid?

options.A: To create a safety net that catches distress early before a full crisis occurs
options.B: To replace professional psychiatric nurses in community hospitals
options.C: To legally license everyday citizens to prescribe mental health drugs
options.D: To reduce the financial budget required for national health insurance

explanation: Training everyday leaders helps spot warning signs early, allowing for fast support before problems escalate. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h6)

question: What is a major risk if a woman hyperventilates too severely during the second stage of labour?

options.A: Rapid increase in the maternal residual lung volume
options.B: Sudden and permanent closure of the maternal airway
options.C: Complete cessation of all uterine contractions
options.D: Reduced blood flow and oxygen delivery to the placenta

explanation: Blowing off too much CO2 constricts blood vessels, which can lower the oxygen flowing to the baby. Coaching mum to breathe calmly prevents this! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T3#GNS121_U7_T3_h5)

question: A pregnant patient asks how to reduce dark patches on her face. What is the best nursing advice?

options.A: Scrub the face vigorously with harsh soap twice a day
options.B: Stop drinking milk immediately to clear skin pigment
options.C: Apply strong bleaching creams prescribed over the counter
options.D: Apply daily sunscreen and wear wide-brimmed hats outdoors

explanation: Sunlight makes facial darkening (melasma) pop out more. Advising sun protection is a simple, effective tip every nursing student should know! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h2)

question: At what point in pregnancy do the very first structures of the nervous system start to form?

options.A: During the final trimester
options.B: During the third week of pregnancy
options.C: Around the fifth month of gestation
options.D: Immediately after birth

explanation: Spot on! Nervous system development starts super early—during the third week of pregnancy—which is why early antenatal care is so important. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T1#GNS211_U3_T1_h1)

question: What do biochemical tests mainly measure to help identify an unknown bacterium?

options.A: The patient's immune antibody response to the infection
options.B: The exact physical length and width of the cell wall
options.C: The specific chemical and metabolic activities of the organism
options.D: The genetic sequence of the organism's outer capsule

explanation: Spot on! These tests check what foods the bacteria can eat or what waste products they make, revealing their identity. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h5)

question: A patient requires skin closure on a forehead laceration that will need stitches removed in five days. Which suture type should the nurse prepare?

options.A: Absorbable gut
options.B: Elastic band material
options.C: Non-absorbable nylon
options.D: Heavy wire suture

explanation: Skin surface closures require non-absorbable materials like nylon so they remain intact until manual removal. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h4)

question: Which body is officially responsible for regulating HMOs in Nigeria?

options.A: National Health Insurance Authority
options.B: Pharmaceutical Council of Nigeria
options.C: Nigerian Medical Association
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NHIA is the federal agency tasked with setting standards, registering, and monitoring all HMOs operating within the country. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why is a speech therapist often called in to help patients with advanced neurodegenerative disorders?

options.A: To teach them foreign languages
options.B: To cure their underlying memory loss
options.C: To help manage swallowing and communication issues
options.D: To improve their walking balance and posture

explanation: Speech therapists do more than just speech—they train and protect the muscles used for swallowing, which stops dangerous choking and aspiration. Fantastic nursing awareness! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T15#GNS222_U3_T15_h6)

question: A client comes to you asking for advice on diet and irregular ovulation. What is the best starting point?

options.A: Focus on whole foods, healthy weight management, and essential micronutrients
options.B: Rely entirely on heavy vitamin supplements instead of eating meals
options.C: Drink large amounts of caffeinated coffee to boost resting metabolism
options.D: Eliminate all carbohydrates completely from your daily meals

explanation: Awesome choice! Real, wholesome food and steady weight management give the body the stable foundation it needs for natural hormonal balance. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T011#GNS227_U2_T011_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal job of a healthy kidney?

options.A: Filtering and breaking down peptide hormones
options.B: Making large amounts of dietary insulin
options.C: Releasing erythropoietin when oxygen is low
options.D: Clearing parathyroid hormone from the blood

explanation: Spot on! Insulin is made by your pancreas, not your kidneys. The kidneys just help clear it out of your system later. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the main focus when managing non-communicable diseases in clinical practice?

options.A: Isolating the patient in a specialized ward to prevent spreading
options.B: Achieving a complete cure within a fourteen-day treatment window
options.C: Administering a short course of antibiotics to kill the pathogen
options.D: Long-term symptom control and prevention of complications

explanation: Correct! Because chronic conditions last a lifetime, our care focuses on keeping symptoms under control, protecting organs, and helping patients live well. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of leadership in community health practice?

options.A: Empowering communities to manage their own health
options.B: Reducing the operational costs of local clinics
options.C: Enforcing strict compliance with national hospital policies
options.D: Directing all medical treatment decisions without input

explanation: Community leadership focuses on working alongside the population so they can eventually direct and sustain their own health improvements. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T2#GNS124_U2_T2_h1)

question: A patient in a disaster zone has a severe head injury, is unresponsive, breathing irregularly, and has no pulse. Which triage category fits best?

options.A: Red
options.B: Black
options.C: Yellow
options.D: Green

explanation: You're doing great. A black tag (or expectant) is used for catastrophic injuries where survival is sadly very unlikely, helping us save resources for those we can help. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h2)

question: What is a key nursing duty when caring for a patient with a metabolic disorder?

options.A: Encouraging the patient to eat unlimited amounts of simple sugars
options.B: Prescribing new metabolic medications to cure the underlying defect
options.C: Replacing all oral nutrition with intravenous fluids permanently
options.D: Monitoring laboratory results and tracking dietary intake closely

explanation: As a nurse, keeping a close eye on lab trends and meals helps you catch sneaky metabolic imbalances before they become emergencies! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h8)

question: What is a major health risk in overcrowded refugee or displaced persons (IDP) camps?

options.A: A sudden surplus of safe drinking water
options.B: Complete elimination of nutritional deficiencies
options.C: Immediate eradication of chronic lifestyle illnesses
options.D: Rapid outbreaks of waterborne and communicable diseases

explanation: Well done! When people live close together with poor sanitation, infections like cholera and measles can spread very quickly. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h2)

question: Which of these is a great example of intrinsic motivation?

options.A: Avoiding a written warning from the director of nursing
options.B: Receiving a monthly cash bonus for perfect attendance
options.C: Finding personal joy and satisfaction in helping a patient recover
options.D: Competing with colleagues for the nurse of the month plaque

explanation: Intrinsic motivation comes from within—like the warm feeling you get when your patient smiles and gets better. No award needed! [learn more](GST321_U1_T18#GST321_U1_T18_h2)

question: What nursing term describes a patient passing less than 400 mL of urine in a full day?

options.A: Hematuria
options.B: Dysuria
options.C: Oliguria
options.D: Polyuria

explanation: You've got it! Oliguria means low urine output. It's an important red flag that tells nurses the kidneys might be stressed or dehydrated. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T6#GNS121_U2_T6_h7)

question: Why must a food handler with a finger cut wear a brightly colored waterproof bandage?

options.A: To prevent the bandage from absorbing water in the sink
options.B: To make it easily visible if it falls off into the food
options.C: To speed up the healing process of the skin wound
options.D: To hide the injury from customers who might feel uncomfortable

explanation: Bright waterproof plasters make it super easy to spot and retrieve the bandage if it accidentally drops into a meal. Smart, right? [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h3)

question: What actually happens during the autoimmune destruction of an endocrine gland?

options.A: A genetic mutation stops hormone production entirely
options.B: An infection blocks the blood supply to the organ
options.C: The immune system attacks and destroys glandular cells
options.D: A benign tumor crowds out normal hormone tissue

explanation: Think of it as friendly fire! The immune system gets confused and mistakenly attacks healthy cells in the gland. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T8#GNS211_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which lab value usually climbs when a patient has failing kidneys and can't clear protein waste?

options.A: Serum potassium levels
options.B: Red blood cell count
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen
options.D: Total body water weight

explanation: Since urea is the main waste product of protein, sluggish kidneys mean urea backs up, causing Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) levels to rise. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h6)

question: How do Electronic Health Records mainly improve teamwork among healthcare professionals?

options.A: By eliminating the need for nurses and doctors to ever speak to each other
options.B: By replacing all physical bedside shift handovers with text messages
options.C: By allowing instant access to updated patient notes across different departments
options.D: By automatically deciding the medical diagnosis for every admitted patient

explanation: Instant digital access means doctors, nurses, and pharmacists can see the same up-to-date information simultaneously, improving coordination of care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which specific nerve fibers in the skin are responsible for sending itch signals to the brain?

options.A: Pacinian touch receptors
options.B: Unmyelinated C-fibers
options.C: Meissner corpuscle endings
options.D: Large myelinated A-alpha fibers

explanation: Unmyelinated C-fibers are specialized nerve endings in our skin that pick up itch (pruritic) signals and carry them to the spinal cord. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h4)

question: How should you write down a patient's story of how an injury happened in their chart?

options.A: Omitting the patient's story to save clinical documentation time
options.B: Writing down personal assumptions about the perpetrator
options.C: Using the patient's exact words in quotation marks
options.D: Summarizing the event using clinical diagnostic slang

explanation: Always use their exact words in quotes! It keeps your notes honest, clear, and legally solid. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T13#GNS312_U4_T13_h3)

question: Why do routine medical checks in schools help find vision and hearing issues early?

options.A: Teachers are trained ophthalmologists and audiologists
options.B: Children rarely complain about mild sensory deficits on their own
options.C: Parents deliberately hide medical test results from school authorities
options.D: Sensory problems only develop while children are inside classrooms

explanation: Exactly! Kids often think everyone sees or hears just like they do, so they won't realize they have a problem unless we check. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T45#GNS214_U1_T45_h4)

question: In a female body, which organs make up the 'gonads' part of the HPG axis?

options.A: The mammary glands
options.B: The fallopian tubes
options.C: The uterus
options.D: The ovaries

explanation: Spot on! Gonads are the primary reproductive organs—testes in males and ovaries in females. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T7#GNS121_U4_T7_h2)

question: Why must nurses always teach postpartum women to clean their perineal area from front to back?

options.A: To stimulate faster contraction of the abdominal wall muscles
options.B: To ensure that lochia stops flowing within the first twenty-four hours
options.C: To prevent spreading bacteria from the anal region into the vagina or wound
options.D: To prevent painful swelling of the lower extremities

explanation: Wiping front to back keeps unwanted germs from the back passage away from healing tears or surgical stitches, preventing nasty infections! Simple hygiene makes a massive difference. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h7)

question: Why do nurses sometimes easily miss mental health struggles in patients with physical disabilities?

options.A: Psychological assessment is outside the legal scope of nursing
options.B: Mental health issues always disappear on their own over time
options.C: Physical symptoms like pain and wounds demand immediate attention
options.D: Patients with disabilities never experience anxiety or depression

explanation: It happens so easily in a busy ward! Because physical needs are loud and urgent, we can unintentionally overlook invisible emotional pain. Keep your eyes open for both! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T14#GNS225_U5_T14_h1)

question: How should a nurse handle someone who argues that there is 'no budget' for a new health project?

options.A: Ignore the stakeholder completely and proceed without their approval
options.B: Provide evidence showing financial losses caused by ignoring the issue
options.C: Offer to pay for the entire project out of the nurse's own salary
options.D: Argue loudly that the government is corrupt and does not care

explanation: Smart move! Showing them how much money the problem is *already* costing them helps turn a 'no budget' excuse into a reason to invest. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h6)

question: Why do airborne diseases require special negative-pressure rooms while droplet diseases do not?

options.A: Airborne particles stay suspended in the air and travel much farther
options.B: Droplet nuclei are too large to pass through standard hospital doors
options.C: Airborne pathogens only survive inside the human bloodstream
options.D: Droplet particles are heavy and require direct physical contact to spread

explanation: Tiny airborne nuclei float on air currents across rooms, whereas heavy droplets quickly drop to the ground within a short distance. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h4)

question: What three conditions make up the dangerous 'lethal triad' in severe trauma?

options.A: Hypotension, hypoxia, and polyuria
options.B: Tachycardia, alkalosis, and dehydration
options.C: Hyperglycemia, fever, and hypertension
options.D: Hypothermia, acidosis, and coagulopathy

explanation: Low body temperature, acid buildup, and poor clotting form a vicious, deadly cycle in major trauma cases. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T4#GNS221_U3_T4_h8)

question: What is a comprehensive community diagnosis?

options.A: A financial audit of local government health clinics
options.B: An in-depth study covering all aspects of health and life in the community
options.C: A quick check of only the children under five years old
options.D: A laboratory test for a single infectious disease

explanation: A comprehensive diagnosis looks at everything from demographics and economics to all available health services. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h3)

question: What does 'test-retest reliability' check in a study?

options.A: Stability of scores over time
options.B: Agreement between two different observers
options.C: Equivalence of two different questionnaire versions
options.D: Internal similarity of survey questions

explanation: Spot on! Test-retest simply means giving the same test to the same people at two different times to see if the scores stay stable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h3)

question: What are those bony bumps that form on the edges of joints in osteoarthritis called?

options.A: Osteoids
options.B: Osteoblasts
options.C: Osteoclasts
options.D: Osteophytes

explanation: Osteophytes are commonly known as bone spurs. They form when the bone tries to repair itself after losing smooth cartilage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T20#GNS222_U1_T20_h2)

question: Why does the baby have to make 'cardinal movements' while coming down the birth canal?

options.A: To stimulate the release of oxytocin from the maternal pituitary gland
options.B: To speed up the latent phase of the first stage of labour
options.C: To prevent the umbilical cord from wrapping around the baby's neck
options.D: To help the fetal head fit through the changing shapes of the maternal pelvis

explanation: The pelvis isn't a straight pipe! The baby has to twist and turn to navigate the different curves safely. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T004#GNS226_U3_T004_h5)

question: What are the three core parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Infection, morbidity, and mortality
options.B: Vector, reservoir, and transmission
options.C: Agent, host, and environment
options.D: Primary, secondary, and tertiary

explanation: Think of disease as a puzzle made of three pieces: the germ (agent), the person (host), and where they live (environment). [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h2)

question: Which IV fluid is the gold standard for fluid resuscitation during the first day of major burn care?

options.A: 5 percent Albumin solution
options.B: Lactated Ringer's solution
options.C: 5 percent Dextrose in Water
options.D: 0.9 percent Normal Saline

explanation: Lactated Ringer's is closest in makeup to our body's own blood plasma, making it the top choice for refilling those empty tanks after a burn. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why do we include a reference list at the end of a report?

options.A: To provide extra reading material for hospitalized patients
options.B: To give proper credit to original authors and avoid plagiarism
options.C: To increase the length of the document for academic grading
options.D: To prove that the researcher read every textbook in the library

explanation: Referencing is about honesty—always give credit to the original authors whose work helped you build yours! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T17#GNS217_U3_T17_h9)

question: Why should a nurse teach a patient NOT to squeeze their buttocks while doing Kegels?

options.A: To avoid raising the patient's blood pressure
options.B: To ensure the correct pelvic floor muscles are being isolated
options.C: To prevent cramping in the leg muscles
options.D: To keep the bladder from emptying too quickly

explanation: Brilliant! Squeezing the glutes or thighs cheats the exercise. We want the actual pelvic sling doing the heavy lifting! [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h8)

question: A mum has strong contractions, but her cervical dilation hasn't changed at all for three hours. What is this called?

options.A: Arrest of dilatation
options.B: Protracted latent phase
options.C: Precipitous delivery
options.D: Normal descent

explanation: Exactly right. When dilation completely halts for two hours or more during active labour, we call it an arrest of dilatation. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T003#GNS226_U3_T003_h3)

question: How do vitamins and minerals often help enzymes do their work?

options.A: They turn into glucose to provide extra energy for the brain.
options.B: They act as coenzymes and cofactors to help enzymes function.
options.C: They slow down metabolism to prevent the body from overheating.
options.D: They replace enzymes when the body runs out of protein.

explanation: Many vitamins and minerals team up with enzymes as coenzymes or cofactors, acting like a key that unlocks the enzyme's full working potential! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T006#GNS227_U1_T006_h6)

question: Why do we measure blood pressure in millimeters of mercury (mmHg)?

options.A: It measures the exact weight of blood inside the heart
options.B: It estimates the total oxygen carried by red blood cells
options.C: It is the standard unit based on historical manometers
options.D: It calculates the chemical composition of plasma

explanation: It's all history! Early blood pressure tools (manometers) actually used columns of liquid mercury, and the mmHg unit stuck around to this day. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T6#GNS111_U2_T6_h1)

question: What is a main difference between personal and organisational objectives?

options.A: Personal goals focus on individual growth, while organisational goals focus on collective institutional success
options.B: Personal goals never involve learning or professional development
options.C: Personal goals are always written by the government, while organisational goals are written by nurses
options.D: Organisational goals only care about individual staff salaries

explanation: Think of it simply: personal goals are about your own growth and pocket, while organisational goals are about the success and health standards of the whole hospital. [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why do nurses focus on empowerment in Family Life Education?

options.A: It forces community members to adopt identical lifestyles
options.B: It ensures that nurses make all final decisions for clients
options.C: It helps learners build critical thinking for better choices
options.D: It prevents individuals from questioning health policies

explanation: Empowerment means giving people the tools to think for themselves so they can make the best health decisions for their own lives. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T46#GNS214_U1_T46_h2)

question: You listen to all four areas of a patient's tummy for five full minutes and hear zero sounds. What does this mean?

options.A: Absent bowel sounds indicating decreased motility
options.B: Normal digestion happening very quietly
options.C: Mild gas trapped in the lower colon
options.D: Hyperactive sounds due to recent eating

explanation: Total silence for a full five minutes is a red flag! It usually means the intestines have slowed right down or stopped moving. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T2#GNS213_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why are bedside nurses so important when it comes to quality improvement projects?

options.A: They make all final hospital policy decisions without physician input.
options.B: They are the only healthcare workers permitted to collect hospital data.
options.C: They are legally required to manage hospital financial budgets.
options.D: They spend the most time observing daily clinical workflows and patient responses.

explanation: Exactly! As bedside nurses, you spend the most time with patients and see how things actually run on the ward every day, making your insights super valuable. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h3)

question: Which major complication do rehabilitation nurses constantly work to prevent?

options.A: Sudden visual impairment
options.B: Spontaneous bone fractures
options.C: Acute myocardial infarction
options.D: Pressure injuries and contractures

explanation: Great job! Because rehab patients often spend a lot of time resting, nurses watch closely to prevent bed sores (pressure injuries) and stiff joints (contractures). [learn more](GNS324_U5_T10#GNS324_U5_T10_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the paired paranasal sinuses?

options.A: Maxillary sinus
options.B: Frontal sinus
options.C: Temporal sinus
options.D: Sphenoid sinus

explanation: The temporal bone does not contain a paranasal sinus; the four paired sinuses are maxillary, frontal, sphenoid, and ethmoid. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why must nursing care for teenagers be gender-responsive?

options.A: Because boys and girls experience different cultural expectations and health risks
options.B: Because male and female bodies require entirely separate hospital buildings
options.C: Because female patients always refuse treatment from male nurses
options.D: Because boys never experience any emotional or psychological health issues

explanation: Gender-responsive care acknowledges that societal roles and biological differences create unique health vulnerabilities for different genders during adolescence. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T4#GNS312_U4_T4_h1)

question: A patient with severe tummy pain walks into the clinic bent forward. What is causing this posture?

options.A: Normal aging changes
options.B: A neurological stroke
options.C: Extreme psychological joy
options.D: Pain and guarding

explanation: This is called 'guarding.' It's a natural, protective reflex where the body curls inward to shield a painful spot from touch or stretch. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is the safest way for a nurse to check the strength and timing of a mum's contractions?

options.A: Ask the patient to guess how long her abdominal pain lasts
options.B: Measure the mother's blood pressure before and after every contraction
options.C: Perform frequent digital vaginal examinations every fifteen minutes
options.D: Palpate the fundus of the uterus with the fingertips over a set period

explanation: Gentle touch on the top of the uterus (the fundus) tells you everything you need to know about contractions without risking infection from too many internal exams. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T004#GNS226_U3_T004_h7)

question: What happens when hospital administrators treat MBO as just a bureaucratic checklist?

options.A: Patient satisfaction increases across all departments
options.B: The hospital saves money on administrative salaries
options.C: Staff quickly lose interest and trust in the process
options.D: Nurses become expert planners overnight

explanation: When MBO lacks genuine leadership commitment and becomes mere paperwork, staff view it as a burden rather than a useful tool. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why do cells in a tissue live surrounded by an extracellular matrix?

options.A: To hold the cells together and help them share a common function
options.B: To generate electrical impulses for the nervous system automatically
options.C: To prevent any fluid from ever moving between the cells
options.D: To completely isolate each cell from its neighbors for protection

explanation: The extracellular matrix acts like mortar in a brick wall, holding the cells together so they can work as a solid team. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: What kind of pain do adjuvant medications like gabapentin usually target?

options.A: Sudden high fever from bacterial infection
options.B: Acute inflammatory joint swelling
options.C: Neuropathic pain from damaged nerves
options.D: Severe stomach cramping from food poisoning

explanation: Gabapentin and similar drugs are originally seizure medicines, but they work wonders for that burning, shooting pain caused by damaged nerves. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T2#GNS223_U5_T2_h4)

question: What does having an 'appreciation for a system' mean in a busy hospital setting?

options.A: Ensuring every single department makes a profit
options.B: Keeping hospital departments strictly separated so no one gets distracted
options.C: Recognizing how different departments depend on each other to reach a common goal
options.D: Giving regular awards to hardworking nursing staff

explanation: Think of a hospital like a football team—pharmacy, lab, and nursing all have to pass the ball to each other to win for the patient! [learn more](GST319_U2_T3#GST319_U2_T3_h2)

question: A researcher spots a few strange blood pressure numbers that look like typos in the database. What is the best first step?

options.A: Ignore the mistakes and run the statistical analysis anyway
options.B: Change the numbers randomly to fit the average reading
options.C: Check the original paper records to verify the correct entry
options.D: Delete all the patient records so they do not ruin the study

explanation: Data cleaning means checking suspicious entries against original source documents rather than guessing or deleting data carelessly. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which special cell type must be present to diagnose Hodgkin Lymphoma?

options.A: Epithelial cells
options.B: Reed-Sternberg cells
options.C: Plasma cells
options.D: Kupffer cells

explanation: Spotting giant, unusual Reed-Sternberg cells under a microscope is the classic giveaway that tells doctors it's Hodgkin Lymphoma! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T9#GNS311_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a barrier to good communication between hospital departments?

options.A: Use of specialized professional jargon
options.B: Physical distance between separate hospital units
options.C: Universal and open departmental transparency
options.D: Rigid hierarchy and power dynamics

explanation: Exactly! Transparency actually builds trust and helps communication flow. Things like heavy jargon, long distances, and strict hierarchies are the real roadblocks. [learn more](GST321_U1_T12#GST321_U1_T12_h3)

question: A nurse accidentally types a patient's heart rate as 12 instead of 120 beats per minute. What primary concept does this error affect?

options.A: Physical network security
options.B: Data quality and validity
options.C: Patient financial billing status
options.D: Hospital building architecture

question: Why is 'closed-loop communication' so important during a chaotic resuscitation?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from having to touch the patient
options.B: It confirms that instructions given by the team leader are clearly heard and executed
options.C: It ensures that family members outside the room stay quiet
options.D: It reduces the need for documentation after the code is over

explanation: Brilliant! Repeating instructions back (like 'Giving 1mg epinephrine now') stops dangerous mistakes when things get loud and fast. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T4#GNS315_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is communication considered a vital part of the IEC approach rather than just giving information?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will take their prescribed medications on time.
options.B: It establishes a two-way dialogue to build trust and address community concerns.
options.C: It allows the nurse to avoid writing formal health reports.
options.D: It eliminates the need for any formal health education classes.

explanation: Communication is a two-way process that fosters trust and helps health workers understand local beliefs and fears. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T2#GNS124_U5_T2_h1)

question: What is the main goal of a community's 'production, distribution, and consumption' function?

options.A: Providing free hospital care to every citizen
options.B: Teaching cultural values to children in school buildings
options.C: Enforcing criminal laws and maintaining local police stations
options.D: Meeting the basic survival and economic needs of members

question: Which of these actions does NOT help promote independence in a visually impaired patient?

options.A: Teaching them to organize clothing by texture and location

options.C: Encouraging the use of a white cane for outdoor travel
options.D: Suggesting talking clocks and large-print books

question: A newly formed community health committee has stopped arguing and is now setting clear operational rules. Which stage of development are they in?

options.A: Storming
options.B: Norming
options.C: Forming
options.D: Adjourning

question: What is the name of the special fund in Nigeria set up to directly support primary healthcare facilities?

options.D: Federal Drug Procurement Account

question: Why is washing hands with soap and water so important before a home blood glucose test?

options.C: Water activates the electronic screen on the meter
options.D: It is the only way to sterilize the testing strip

question: What makes true sexual consent valid?

options.B: Written permission signed by both set of parents
options.C: The freedom to say no without negative consequences
options.D: Physical dominance by one partner over the other

question: What is the typical time frame for an immediate drug reaction to appear after administration?

options.C: Between three and seven days
options.D: After two weeks of treatment

question: Why do nurses appreciate capnography during patient sedation?

options.C: It doesn't need batteries or power to work
options.D: It checks blood pressure much faster than a cuff

question: What does continuous professional development help maintain in a nursing team?

options.A: Fewer working hours for night shifts
options.B: A lower overall patient bed capacity

options.D: Up-to-date clinical knowledge and best practices

question: Why is teaching patients to read food labels a great nursing skill for fat management?

options.D: It means they never need to see a dietitian again
